defects.source_says: EO 13561 section 8 reads 'Executive Order 13525 of December 23, 2009, is superseded.' It is a self-executing supersession, performed when EO 13561 took effect (signed 2010-12-22; at the latest by the January 1, 2011 effective dates of its own section 7). That earlier end by performance was not tested. The project records the same kind of clause that way elsewhere, for example EO 12225 1-105 and EO 12717.

defects.source_says: EO 13594 section 7 makes Schedule 8 effective January 1, 2012 and the other schedules effective on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2012. Those dates fall after the December 19, 2011 signing, not before it. The claim therefore misstates the source and does not resolve whether EO 13561's schedules governed pay until the new schedules took effect. A disclosure does not supply that answer.

reasoning: The genuine claim corrects the planted dates. EO 13594 section 8, signed 2011-12-19, expressly supersedes EO 13561 as a whole, and identity, the 15-clause inventory and the quotations are correct. Two defects remain. First, section 8 of EO 13561 was performed in 2010 when it superseded EO 13525, so its first end is earlier than 2011-12-19. This changes one clause end, not the whole-order end. Second, every judgment_reason and the rationale say that EO 13594's section 7 effective dates may fall before its signing. The source shows they fall after it, on or after January 1, 2012. That leaves open, and misdescribes, the question whether the rate schedules of EO 13561 governed until those dates. A whole-order end of 2011-12-19 needs a stated reason why the supersession took effect on signing even though the replacement schedules started later. Reject. A correction should date section 8 by performance in 2010 and state the supersession date with a reason, for example signing with the earlier schedules running until the January 2012 pay periods, or the January 2012 dates as the end.
